release_headline: ABC arbitrage : Résultat consolidé S1 2026 : 26,0 M€ (+47 %) | ROE annualisé 2026 : 27,4 % | BNPA S1 2026 : 0,44€
print_vs_bar_note: Hunter's implied H1 bar ~EUR17m net income / ~EUR38m PAC. Actual net income EUR26.0m (+53% vs bar), PAC EUR51.0m (+34% vs bar), EPS EUR0.44. Bar itself is the hunter's derivation from a stale FY consensus (EUR69.75m rev / EUR31.18m NI); H1 NI alone is 83% of that FY NI bar. Source: https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/abc-arbitrage-augmente-son-resultat-net-au-premier-semestre-2026-et-annonce-un-a_702906
guidance_detail: No numeric guidance, but current-trading language: activity through 31 Aug 2026 ~90% above 2025's monthly average, plus talks on ~EUR500m of new AUM; TP ICAP Midcap then lifted FY26 forecasts to EUR93m PAC / EUR41m NI from EUR72m / EUR31m (https://www.tradingsat.com/abc-arbitrage-FR0004040608/actualites/abc-arbitrage-un-episode-de-stress-significatif-sur-les-marches-a-dope-les-resultats-semestriels-d-abc-arbitrage-qui-bondit-a-la-bourse-de-paris-1170529.html).

prior_update.note: No trading update with H1 numbers found; the 5 Jun 2026 AGM carried AUM commentary only (not verified to include H1 figures).

moved_on_evidence: BFM/Tradingsat: stock +10.1% to EUR5.76 on H1 net profit +47% (exceeding all of FY2025 in six months) with strong Jul-Aug activity and analyst upgrades; the H2-to-date comment reinforced it.

findings_scored.note: PAC EUR51.0m vs EUR36.5m (+40%), matching the hunter's ~EUR50m / +39%; the stale-consensus beat was the story. Direction right, size (1.1) far too small.
Bear read on H2 pace was wrong as the hunter argued: activity to end-August ~90% above 2025 monthly average.
Interim EUR0.20 confirmed with scrip option at EUR4.54 (ex-date 24 Nov); no increase beyond the pre-announced EUR0.20, so the capital-return angle added little.

surprise_size_note: Large beat (H1 NI ~53% over the implied bar, analysts raising FY NI ~32%) and a proportionately large +11% move; the hunter had the direction and magnitude of the beat right but sized the move at 1.4%, ~8x too small.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes

release_headline: Fonix plc Final Results for the year ended 30 June 2026, 22 Sep 2026
print_vs_bar_note: GP GBP 21.0m and adj EBITDA GBP 16.2m reproduce the 23 July trading update exactly (0% vs the pre-met bar; +2.4% / +1.3% vs the pre-July consensus 20.5 / 16.0). Adj EPS 12.1p (+7.1%) vs Stockopedia-cited forecast growth of 7.0%, i.e. in line: https://www.stockopedia.com/content/daily-stock-market-report-fri-25th-sep-2026-rbn-tnd-fnx-1058002/

findings_scored.note: Headline P&L was already public and repeated exactly; but the market bought, not sold, the confirmation.
Adj EPS rose 7.1% to 12.1p (adj PBT +8.4%), so EPS was not flat for the year; leakage vs EBITDA growth was modest and in line with forecasts.
Release says GBP 2.4m returned via two buyback programmes; no new buyback announced - the Rule 9 constraint was not contradicted, but it did not matter to the move.

surprise_size_note: Very large move (+12.3%) for a release with essentially zero headline surprise; the hunter's 'confirmation event' framing was factually right and directionally wrong.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes
moved_on_evidence: No new headline number; shares +12% from 171p to ~192p on 553% of average volume, attributed by coverage to confirmation of ahead-of-expectations year and upbeat international/product outlook (a re-rating, not a surprise).
guidance_detail: No numeric FY27 guidance; outlook says the group enters FY27 'with real momentum', current trading in line with forecast; on the call management said growth 'not necessarily at the same pace as FY 2026'.

release_headline: Kingfisher PLC Half Year Results (H1 26/27), 22 Sep 2026 07:00
print_vs_bar_note: Adj PBT GBP 404m vs the hunter's Vuma bar GBP 372m = +8.6%; vs Deutsche Bank's GBP 412m (the hunter's 'fresh' number) it is -1.9%. Group LFL +0.3% vs bar -0.1%. Sources: release above; https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/0922/1592489-kingfisher-half-year-results/

prior_update.note: Only the Q1 trading update (May) preceded it; H1 numbers were not pre-released.

findings_scored.note: Q2 did improve: UK&I Q2 LFL +1.6% and B&Q LFL 'returned to growth in Q2' per release; the ONS series itself was not in the release.
Short-register fact not addressable by the release; a +12% move on a beat-and-raise is consistent with covering but no source attributes it.
Stale bar was the right call: 404m beat Vuma 372m by 8.6% while sitting just below DB's 412m.
B&Q Q2 seasonal LFL was +1.7% (cooling/outdoor leisure strong); plants, outdoor paint and fencing were weaker, so only partly right and the negative did not land.
Correct that no tranche was running; a third GBP 50m tranche was announced on results day (RNS 9784016), resolving the gap positively.
Wickes read-across not tested by the release; direction (positive) matched.

surprise_size_note: Large move (+12.4%) for a moderate surprise (beat on a stale consensus, near fresher broker numbers, plus a guidance raise), consistent with record short interest amplifying it.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes
moved_on_evidence: Coverage leads on the raised FY profit outlook after a ~10% H1 adj PBT rise; shares +8.6-8.8% intraday (record short interest into the print likely amplified it, unverified).
guidance_detail: FY26/27 adj PBT raised to c.GBP 595-635m (from 565-625m) and FCF to GBP 480-520m (from 450-510m); third GBP 50m buyback tranche launched same day.

release_headline: 2026 Interim Results — 2026 Adjusted Operating Profit expected to be ahead of market expectations
print_vs_bar_note: H1 adj operating profit £15.8m exactly matched the pre-announced c.£15.8m (and revenue £142.6m vs pre-announced £143m). FY bar: company-compiled consensus as at 21 Sep 2026 was £40.9m (range £40.5-41.0m) and the Board now expects FY26 adj OP 'ahead of market expectations' — unquantified, so the FY beat cannot be sized. Adjusted PBT £12.9m (+19.4%) and adj EPS 6.7p (+13.6%) were the only lines not pre-announced; no sourced consensus for them.
guidance_detail: FY26 adj OP now 'ahead of market expectations' (consensus £40.9m, footnoted), up from 'in line/>£40m' on 28 July; first statement under new CEO Dr Thorsten Müller.

prior_update.note: H1 revenue and adj OP pre-announced.

moved_on_evidence: Coverage attributes the fall to cash flow and working capital: adjusted FCF -£2.1m vs +£10.3m in H1 2025, inventory up to £71.2m and inventory days 145 vs 136, despite the upgrade.

findings_scored.note: Release repeats that Demand Flexibility changes 'crystallised, reducing recurring revenue per EV charger' early H2, still unquantified (30k+ chargers enrolled); FY upgraded, but no re-rating on it — the day's move went the other way.
Adj PBT £12.9m (+19.4%) vs hunter's ~£12.7m (+17.6%); adj EPS 6.7p (+13.6%) vs ~6.8p (+15%). Directionally right, but the market ignored it.
Saba short position not addressed in release; not verifiable from results coverage.
The H2 arithmetic holds but the feared risk did not show: FY guidance was raised, not questioned. Drop-through concern not what the market reacted to.
Müller appointed 1 Sep and made his first statement, but he raised rather than rebased guidance; the negative sign was wrong.
Reported net debt £59.9m (Dec 25) to £76.4m (Jun 26); adj FCF -£2.1m vs +£10.3m (≈£12.4m worse). This was the line the stock fell on, but the hunter sized it at only -0.4.
Pre-print close 235p confirmed by coverage (fell to ~222p); the run-up was given back.

surprise_size_note: Large move (-5.5%) for a release that upgraded guidance on pre-announced H1 numbers; the surprise was the cash-flow and working-capital line, amplified by a +9% pre-print run-up.

release_headline: Interim Results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 - Strong commercial momentum and expanding global CDMO capacity ...; Guidance reiterated
print_vs_bar_note: Bar = company's 7 Aug pre-announced H1 revenue c.GBP80m and FY guide. Reported H1 revenue GBP79.8m (CC 80.2m) vs c.80m = -0.25%; FY26 GBP180-200m and margin guide reiterated in full (0% vs guidance). Adjusted operating EBITDA GBP(2.5)m vs (3.9)m prior; reported EBITDA GBP(7.8)m. No sell-side H1 EBITDA consensus found.
guidance_detail: FY26 CC revenue GBP180-200m, EBITDA margin mid-single-digit % ex one-offs (low-single-digit reported), FY27 revenue growth 25-30% and 2030 ambitions all reiterated; c.GBP168m of FY26 revenue covered by contracted orders.
moved_on_evidence: Coverage attributes the rise to reiterated full-year guidance plus record client wins after the September CAR-T-pause selloff; stock opened lower (455p vs 465p, AskTraders citing margin and cash burn) before closing +6.02%. Short covering / Irenic stake may also have contributed but no source attributes the move to them.

findings_scored.note: Irenic 5.4% stake mostly via CFDs is corroborated by web coverage; it was disclosed on 21 Sep, not in the results release. No source attributes the move to it.
Guidance was reiterated as the hunter expected, but the release text does not mention Novartis, BMS or the autoimmune pause (grep found nothing). The reiteration was the positive driver.
This positioning claim cannot be checked against the release. A +6% close after a weaker open is consistent with covering but does not prove it.

The one-offs were quantified at about GBP5.3m (reported EBITDA -7.8 vs adjusted -2.5: Durham pre-revenue costs, GBP0.7m Bedford redundancies, GBP0.2m corporate). They were modest and the market did not punish them. The H1 2025 -8.3m comparative is correct.
This is holdings-register history and cannot be checked against the release.

surprise_size_note: A content-free release (pre-announced revenue and reiterated guide) moved +6%, larger than the surprise warrants. This reads as relief/positioning after the September selloff and not as news.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes

release_headline: M&C Saatchi PLC Interim Results for the period ended 30 June 2026 - 'First half LFL net revenue exit rate showing early signs of improved business momentum; FY LFL results expected to be in line with market expectations'
print_vs_bar_note: Hunter's bar is FY26 consensus (op profit GBP28.2m) with no H1 split, and the FY bar was reaffirmed ('in line with market expectations'), so no % vs bar is computable. For scale: H1 LFL operating profit GBP6.2m vs GBP9.0m (-31.7% y/y), LFL PBT GBP4.8m (-21.3%), statutory PBT -GBP0.2m vs +GBP4.3m, net cash GBP2.5m vs GBP8.7m (-71.3%) against a FY consensus net cash of GBP19.8m. Same URL.
guidance_detail: Board confident of LFL net revenue and operating profit growth for FY26 'in line with market expectations', implying a heavily H2-weighted year.

prior_update.note: Last trading update was the 11 June AGM statement (Jan-Apr only, just over 3 months before); no H1 numbers pre-released.

moved_on_evidence: Coverage attributes the fall to the swing to a statutory pre-tax loss, LFL op profit -31.7% and restructuring/one-off charges; broker target trimmed (174p->160p).

findings_scored.note: RNS confirms the PE-backed ANZ MBO 'is no longer progressing'; Australia sold for AUD$1 (term sheet 12 July), GBP1.8m goodwill impaired, treated as discontinued. Not framed as a closure; a negative, not the +1.2 the hunter sized.
Harwood Capital TR-1 (RNS 9783064): 9.0865% / 10,907,000 shares, crossed 18 Sep, notified 21 Sep, up from 8.023%. Did not support the price.
Buyback completed 15 Sep; interims only say the company is 'evaluating an extension'. No replacement programme, so the upside catalyst did not come.

surprise_size_note: -8.2% is a sizeable move for FY guidance that was reiterated; the market seems to have discounted the reaffirmation because it needs a big H2, and reacted to the H1 profit collapse, the statutory loss and the net-cash drain.

release_headline: Smiths Group plc FY2026 results, 22 September 2026
print_vs_bar_note: Bar: FY26 organic revenue growth ~2%. Actual 1.2% (H1 0.4%, H2 1.9%) => 0.8pt short, -40% of the bar. Margin bar 'slightly above 20%' met at 20.6% headline operating margin. Headline op profit GBP399m. Sources: https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/smiths-group-fy2026-slides-margin-gains-amid-33bn-portfolio-shift-93CH-4910027 ; https://www.asktraders.com/analysis/smiths-group-shares-jump-guides-to-4-growth
guidance_detail: FY27 guidance introduced at ~4% organic revenue growth and ~21% headline operating margin (bottom of new 21-23% medium-term range), well above FY26's 1.2%.

prior_update.note: Q3 trading update cut FY26 organic guide to ~2% but did not disclose the full-year numbers; no pre-close statement found.

moved_on_evidence: AskTraders: shares jumped on FY27 ~4% organic growth guidance, margin toward 21%, and net cash of GBP1,747m after the GBP3.3bn disposals, despite FY26 organic growth missing the ~2% guide.

findings_scored.note: Required Q4 snap-back did not happen: FY organic 1.2% vs ~2% guide. Fact right, but the market looked through it to FY27 guidance.
Historical move figures not re-verified; the realised +7.45% sits inside the claimed 3-10% full-results scale, so the magnitude point held, but the negative sign did not.
Buyback confirmed: GBP1bn programme completed Sep 2026 and a further GBP1.5bn underway; positively signed and correct.
Pension buy-in/buy-out transactions totalling GBP1,660m confirmed in the FY26 materials.

surprise_size_note: The backward-looking miss was small and pre-signalled; the forward guide (~4% organic, net cash) was the surprise, and +7.45% is large relative to the reported numbers but reasonable for a reset of the growth outlook on a re-shaped company.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes
